clue.text: Meant part to be thrown out to make room

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are thrown out of order and reassembled

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone wants a piece discarded to free up some space.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be thrown out' tells you to rearrange MEANT and PART together.
explanation.definitionFit: A dwelling of rooms, or in older usage a single chamber, so the word can stand for a room.

clue.text: Met poor constituents to give aid

indicators.note: the letters of the two words are treated as raw ingredients to be recombined

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A meeting with the needy, whose voters are helped by their MP.
explanation.walkthrough: 'constituents' is read as the component letters of MET and POOR, rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: To help something forward or further its progress is to back and assist it.

clue.text: The language of love

explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the family of languages descended from Latin, such as French and Italian; the other is a love affair or amorous feeling.

clue.text: It's top gear for the Spanish woman!

definitions.text: It's top gear for the Spanish woman!

parts.words: It's top gear for the Spanish woman!
parts.note: top gear is literally headwear: a lace scarf worn over the head and shoulders by women in Spain

explanation.surface: A fashion line about the best clothes for a señora.
explanation.walkthrough: 'top gear' suggests the finest outfit or a car's gear, but means what goes on top of the head.
explanation.definitionFit: This is the traditional lace head covering, often over a high comb, worn by Spanish women.

clue.text: Mannerisms of drunken artist…

indicators.note: the drunk word staggers about, so its letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: The habits of a painter who has had too much to drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'drunken' asks for ARTIST to be rearranged; the ellipsis links to the next clue only in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Distinguishing habits or characteristics are a person's typical mannerisms.

clue.text: … an artist who was an arresting fellow

explanation.walkthrough: John Constable was an English landscape painter; a constable is a British police officer.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is the English painter of The Hay Wain; the other is a police officer who makes arrests.

clue.text: Offering a good man support without point, coloured

parts.note: ST, short for saint, is the usual crossword good man

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so one piece wraps the other

parts.note: aid is help or support
NE, north-east, is a compass point

explanation.surface: Giving a virtuous person help in a pointless way, now tinted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' means outside here: AID goes round NE to make AINED.
explanation.definitionFit: Something dyed or tinted has been given a colour.

clue.text: Calling for vegetables also-a stone

parts.note: greens are leafy vegetables
and means also or in addition

explanation.surface: Someone asking for leafy veg and a pebble as well.
explanation.definitionFit: A greenish sandstone rich in glauconite, so a type of rock.

clue.text: A list including duck and fowl

indicators.note: the list takes the other piece inside it

parts.note: a roster is a list of names on duty
a duck is a score of nothing in cricket, so the letter O

explanation.surface: A register of birds that has both ducks and chickens on it.
explanation.walkthrough: 'duck' is the cricketing zero, O, not a bird.
explanation.definitionFit: A male chicken, the cock bird, is a domestic fowl.

clue.text: Favouring fine porcelain production

parts.note: to be for something is to favour it
Ming is the Chinese dynasty famed for its porcelain

explanation.surface: A preference for expensive Chinese china being made.
explanation.definitionFit: Making or shaping something is its creation, a gerund meaning the act of producing.

clue.text: Encourage popular feature of the church

parts.note: in means fashionable or popular
a spire is the tall pointed tower on a church

explanation.surface: A church's tower praised as a popular landmark.
explanation.definitionFit: To stir someone with enthusiasm or confidence is to motivate them.

clue.text: Blunt expression of anti-Conservatism?

explanation.walkthrough: In British politics the Conservatives are the right; 'down with the right' is a cry against them.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is frank and outspoken; the other reads the word as a slogan, down meaning away with and right the Tory party.

clue.text: Axe the chat show

indicators.note: show is read as a verb: display these letters in a new arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A demand to cancel a television talk programme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Axe' looks like a verb meaning cancel, and 'chat show' like a TV programme; 'show' is the anagram signal for THE CHAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A small short-handled chopping tool, so a kind of hand axe.

clue.text: They're analytical, like a detective-story writer

parts.note: as means like, in the same way
Dorothy L. Sayers wrote the Lord Peter Wimsey mysteries

explanation.surface: People who think logically are compared to a crime novelist.
explanation.definitionFit: These people test metals and ores to find their composition, which is chemical analysis.

clue.text: Certain about exercise bringing remission

indicators.note: one piece goes round the other

parts.note: real means certain or genuine
PE is physical education, school exercise

explanation.surface: A doctor sure that working out has led to a patient's recovery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'remission' looks medical but means cancellation, as of a law.
explanation.definitionFit: Revoking a law is a remission in the sense of cancelling or annulling it.

clue.text: Fortified so, a sheepish creature split

parts.note: a ram is a male sheep, so a creature of the sheep kind
parted means split or divided

explanation.surface: A timid creature divided, though strengthened.
explanation.definitionFit: Walled with defensive earthworks or bulwarks, and so strengthened against attack.

clue.text: Letters written by a fool about a buccaneer

indicators.note: the first piece goes round the second

parts.note: an ass is a foolish person
a pirate is a buccaneer

explanation.surface: Correspondence penned by an idiot concerning a seafaring raider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letters' suggests correspondence, but means sounds such as H, pronounced with a breath.
explanation.definitionFit: Breathed sounds like H are speech sounds written as single alphabet characters.

clue.text: Chaste eccentric requiring cash bag

indicators.note: eccentric means odd or off-centre, so the letters are put out of order

parts.note: L stands for the pound, from Latin libra, a unit of cash

explanation.surface: A pure but odd person who needs money in a purse.
explanation.walkthrough: 'eccentric' rearranges CHASTE; L is the pound sign's letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A shoulder-strapped school case is a kind of bag.

clue.text: Lead door specially made for the Treasury

indicators.note: the letters are made into something new, a fresh arrangement

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A heavy metal door custom-built for the government finance department.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the Treasury' looks like the UK finance ministry, but means a fabled store of riches.
explanation.definitionFit: The legendary South American city of gold is a storehouse of wealth.

clue.text: Recommend work in plain language!

indicators.note: one piece goes inside the other

parts.note: prose is ordinary language as opposed to verse
op, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Advising someone to write their job in simple words.
explanation.definitionFit: To put forward or suggest a plan is to advise it.

clue.text: The spare pressman relied on others

parts.note: spare means thin or lean
ED, editor, is the crossword newspaperman

explanation.surface: A thin journalist who depended on colleagues.
explanation.definitionFit: To have depended or rested on someone for support.

clue.text: Some upstart is tearing into a performer

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A jumped-up newcomer rushing at a stage entertainer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'tearing into' looks like attacking; the run sits across upstART IS TEaring.
explanation.definitionFit: A professional entertainer such as a singer or dancer.

clue.text: Come to a sensible conclusion?

parts.note: read literally, a finish that is shrewd: a conclusion that is clever, describing something arranged by its tip foremost

explanation.surface: Asking whether one has reached a reasonable decision.
explanation.walkthrough: The word splits into a finish and shrewd; its real sense is with the tip first or lengthways.
explanation.definitionFit: With the tip forward or end to end, lengthways rather than sideways.

clue.text: This is a little bit soft-object

parts.note: P is piano, soft in music
an article is an object or thing

explanation.surface: A small piece of a pliable item.
explanation.definitionFit: A minute fragment or speck of matter.

clue.text: Left a temporary dwelling unobserved

parts.note: a tent is a shelter put up for a short stay

explanation.surface: Someone left a campsite without being seen.
explanation.definitionFit: Hidden and not yet apparent, so not noticed.

clue.text: The time for maximum exposure on the beach!

definitions.text: The time for maximum exposure on the beach!

parts.words: The time for maximum exposure on the beach!
parts.note: suggests sunbathing, but means when the sea has gone furthest out, leaving the most sand uncovered

explanation.surface: Advice on the best time for sunbathing at the seaside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'exposure' hints at sun on skin; it is the sand exposed by the receding sea.
explanation.definitionFit: When the sea is at its lowest ebb, the greatest stretch of shore is uncovered.

clue.text: Cloth worker about fifty getting set again

indicators.note: the cloth-and-worker pair goes round the numeral

parts.note: rep is a ribbed fabric
the ant is the crossword's worker insect
L is the Roman numeral for fifty

explanation.surface: A textile employee aged about fifty getting ready again.
explanation.definitionFit: To put plants back into the soil, setting them once more.

clue.text: Sharp-tongued accountant-American jerk

parts.note: CA is a chartered accountant
a tic is an involuntary jerk

explanation.surface: A bitter accountant from the States, a real idiot.
explanation.walkthrough: 'jerk' suggests a fool but means a twitch.
explanation.definitionFit: Biting or scathing in speech, so cutting with words.

clue.text: Sneer at models from the Orient

indicators.note: models is a verb here: shapes these letters into a new form

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Mocking fashion models who come from Asia.
explanation.walkthrough: 'models' looks like a noun but is the verb rearranging SNEER AT.
explanation.definitionFit: Of or from the East, where Asia lies.

clue.text: Kitchen equipment the beginner can put back-to front

indicators.note: the pieces come in the opposite order to the clue, the second placed ahead

parts.note: a can is a tin
an opener is one who begins something

explanation.surface: A novice cook can turn the kitchen gadgets around.
explanation.walkthrough: 'put back-to front' swaps the clue's order of OPENER and TIN.
explanation.definitionFit: A gadget for cutting open food cans in the kitchen.
